description:
memory.rs:670 (and 277 in seed_object, 163 in objects_mut, 188 in aux_mut) — every write path silently does:

  inner.known_accounts.insert(account_id.as_ref().to_owned());

The comment at line 666-669 calls out the intent: 'silently auto-register so seed_object + create flow without explicit register_account calls in tests does not error spuriously'.

Two problems:

1. The handler at calendar.rs:65-71 (and every other /set handler) calls backend.account_exists() FIRST and short-circuits to accountNotFound if it returns false. The MemoryBackend's account_exists at memory.rs:393-396 reads known_accounts. So if a test creates a MemoryBackend WITHOUT with_account() or register_account(), then directly calls backend.create_object(), the create proceeds — but if it had gone through the dispatcher, accountNotFound would have fired. The two code paths behave inconsistently. The 'silent auto-register' on the backend method makes the backend more permissive than the handler.

2. Production-grade backends MUST NOT auto-register accounts on write — that is a security boundary issue (a request that bypasses the handler's account_exists check would create accounts the operator never authorized). A consumer who reads MemoryBackend as a study example and copies the 'auto-register inside create_object' pattern into a SQL backend has introduced a subtle privilege bug.

The fix is to NOT auto-register inside the backend write methods, and require tests to call with_account() or register_account() explicitly. The 'spurious test failure' the comment alludes to is a feature, not a bug — it ensures the test fixture matches what the handler will check.

Make the test ergonomics nicer instead: add a 'MemoryBackend::new_with_account_and_seeds([(type, id, value)])' helper or similar.

P2. Real maintenance burden if this pattern propagates to other backends.
title: MemoryBackend in-band auto-register of accounts on first write masks accountNotFound contract
